brief: Goldman's US equities desk reads Nov 6 as a healthy bounce led by Semis (+3.5%), not a pure beta squeeze, though HT activity was quiet into the weekend, mostly sentiment-checking with little follow-through. TMT flow was more balanced than the prior day's clearer AI sell skew, Semis supply offset by some fresh demand. Hedge funds finished net buyers, driven by a broad short-covering bid across sectors and macro expressions in a top-down session where ETFs made up over 37% of volume versus a 28% ytd average, so the buying reads as covering, not fresh risk-taking. That reading is reinforced by Prime data: US equities were modestly net sold this week, led by the largest single-stock net selling in four months, partly offset by Macro Products buying; Info Tech was the most net-sold sector globally and in the US, on par with the largest Tech-selling weeks on record, and four of the top five such weeks came in the past five months. L/S gross leverage fell 8.7pts, the largest weekly drop since Covid, to 207.5%; net leverage fell 3.7pts to 43.3% (0th pct, five years). Next week brings CPI (Tue), PPI (Fri), earnings, and a 2.48% straddle to next Friday's close.
